headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risks from shared file-based handoff; no direct data-leak or capability-conflict evidence.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Great Expectations ingests and writes validation files/documentation, while Plane accepts file uploads and stores files/notes. That creates a plausible file-based handoff where Plane content could be treated as trusted input by Great Expectations or vice versa. No direct parser evidence exists, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Plane file uploads are used to pass instructions or markup into Great Expectations validation inputs
IF Great Expectations consumes uploaded or shared files as trusted configuration or test content
mitigations: Restrict handoff files to a dedicated, read-only folder
Strip executable markup from uploaded notes before ingestion
Use a naming convention that separates data files from instruction files
Review one sample handoff file manually before enabling automation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Great Expectations touches data sources, validation results, and documentation, but has network egress none. Plane has broad egress and file uploads, yet no shared workspace or shared OAuth principal is shown. The pair can still leak via manual file transfer, but the blast radius is limited and not default.
conditions: IF sensitive validation results are manually uploaded from Great Expectations into Plane
IF Plane users attach files containing data sources or validation outputs
mitigations: Avoid uploading raw validation outputs to Plane
Redact sensitive columns before sharing reports
Store sensitive artifacts in a separate restricted folder
Limit Plane attachments to summaries only

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Great Expectations can install packages and write local files; Plane cannot write filesystem and supports multiple instances. There is no shared mutable resource or overlapping write scope in the profiles, so direct conflict is unlikely. Any contention would require an external shared directory not evidenced here.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external writable directory
IF an operator grants Plane filesystem write access outside the profile
mitigations: Keep each agent in a separate working directory
Disable shared mounts between the two services
Use per-agent temp directories
Document ownership of any shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: Great Expectations produces validation results that Plane can store as files, notes, or issues. If Plane treats those outputs as authoritative without a verification step, bad checks or stale results can cascade into tasking or scheduling decisions. The interaction is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly observed, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Plane issues or notes are created directly from Great Expectations validation output
IF no human review occurs before Plane records the result as authoritative
mitigations: Require a human approval step before creating Plane issues
Attach the original validation query alongside the result
Mark imported results as provisional
Add a checklist item to verify source data freshness

E_compliance.rationale: Great Expectations is a local data-engineering tool with no network egress, while Plane is a self-hosted issue tracker with broad egress and file uploads. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, but they do show different handling patterns for the same data classes, so the compliance risk is limited and operational.
conditions: IF regulated data from Great Expectations is uploaded into Plane
IF Plane is deployed in a jurisdiction or retention regime different from the source data
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Plane attachments
Set a short retention policy for uploaded files
Use self-hosted Plane in the same jurisdiction as the source data
Record a data-handling policy for validation artifacts
